packet.headline_seed: OpenAI limits GPT-5.6 rollout after government request, says restrictions shouldn’t be the norm

what: OpenAI limits GPT-5.6 rollout after government request, says restrictions shouldn’t be the norm

clean_source_blocks.text: “We don’t believe this kind of government access process should become the long-term default,” says OpenAI. “It keeps the best tools from users, developers, enterprises, cyber defenders, and global partners who need them.”

“We don’t believe this kind of government access process should become the long-term default,” OpenAI wrote in its blog post. “It keeps the best tools from users, developers, enterprises, cyber defenders, and global partners who need them. We are taking this short-term step because we believe it is the strongest path to broader availability in the coming weeks, while we work with the Administration to develop the cyber Executive Order framework and a repeatable process for future model releases.”

While allowing that the “limited” release for GPT-5.6 will help ensure “the strongest path to broader availability in the coming weeks,” OpenAI warned that “this kind of government access process … keeps the best tools from users, developers, enterprises, cyber defenders, and global partners who need them.” Anticipating the concerns raised by Anthropic’s Fable and Mythos models, which are said to have breached sensitive national security systems “in hours,” OpenAI went to great lengths to detail GPT 5.6’s “layered” safeguards, including against jailbreaking and “real-world adversarial pressure.” OpenAI said it anticipates that GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna will be released “soon” to general users. But just as Claude Fable and Mythos remain in a regulatory limbo, it’s not at all clear when the U.S. government will give the all-clear for the GPT-5.6 series to go into wide release.

OpenAI is delaying the public release of its next generation of AI models, GPT-5.6, at the request of Trump’s White House, the company confirmed on Friday. OpenAI said it would first share the models with a small set of customers, which will be preapproved by the US government. It will then work with the administration to slowly expand access. OpenAI is not happy about this, according to a person familiar with the company’s thinking, but believes the delay and government approval process is only temporary. In a blog post, the company said it hopes it will be able to make GPT-5.6 available to everyone in the coming weeks. OpenAI’s plans to delay its next generation of AI models at the Trump administration’s request was first reported by The Information.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
OpenAI is limiting the release of its newest AI models to a “small group of trusted partners” at the behest of the U.S. government, the company said Friday.

The next generation GPT-5.6 lineup includes Sol, its flagship model; Terra, a more balanced model for everyday use; and Luna, a faster, lower cost option. Although Sol is the company’s most powerful mode, the Trump administration has restricted the release of all three. OpenAI said the preview is limited to partners “whose participation has been shared with the government.”

---

[Lähde: Wired]
OpenAI is delaying the public release of its next generation of AI models, GPT-5.6, at the request of Trump’s White House, the company confirmed on Friday. OpenAI said it would first share the models with a small set of customers, which will be preapproved by the US government. It will then work with the administration to slowly expand access.

OpenAI is not happy about this, according to a person familiar with the company’s thinking, but believes the delay and government approval process is only temporary. In a blog post, the company said it hopes it will be able to make GPT-5.6 available to everyone in the coming weeks. OpenAI’s plans to delay its next generation of AI models at the Trump administration’s request was first reported by The Information.

“We don’t believe this kind of government access process should become the long-term default,” OpenAI wrote in its blog post. “It keeps the best tools from users, developers, enterprises, cyber defenders, and global partners who need them. We are taking this short-term step because we believe it is the strongest path to broader availability in the coming weeks, while we work with the Administration to develop the cyber Executive Order framework and a repeatable process for future model releases.”

Earlier this month, President Trump signed an executive order that aimed to address the cybersecurity concerns of powerful new AI models. The order said the White House would create a “voluntary process” for AI labs to share their models with the government 30 days ahead of a broader release. The mandate included a carve-out, saying the US government would not turn its voluntary process into a de facto licensing regime for AI model releases. But in its Friday briefing, OpenAI executives said no such voluntary framework exists yet. As a result, the frontier AI labs are in a very weird interim period, where working with the US government on your AI model launch doesn’t seem all that voluntary.

The White House is asking OpenAI to stagger the release of its AI models just two weeks after it sent an export control directive to Anthropic, which prompted the company to take its most advanced AI models offline for all customers. Anthropic’s spat with the White House is still unresolved, and some of the company’s own employees are still barred from using its most advanced AI models.

[Lähde: PCWorld]
The U.S. government ban on Anthropic’s powerful Fable and Mythos models has everybody spooked. That’s why it’s a little surprising that OpenAI, Anthropic’s biggest rival, is slowly rolling out its latest and most powerful GPT models.

Yes, the GPT-5.6 series of models is here, but not for everyone. It comes in three flavors: the flagship Sol model, the everyday Terra, and the fast-and-efficient Luna. Those models map roughly to the Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku configuration of Anthropic’s Claude models.

That said, Sol is really more of a competitor to Fable and Mythos, the two Claude models that were slapped with expert restrictions by the Trump Administration earlier this month over fears they were too dangerous for broad release.

Like Fable and particularly Mythos (which was restricted to only a small group of handpicked users and organizations even before the U.S. ban), GPT-5.6 Sol is being billed as OpenAI’s “strongest model yet,” complete with robust coding, biology, and cybersecurity capabilities.

But while Anthropic put Claude Fable into general release before being ordered to pull it down days later, OpenAI said its GPT-5.6 models will start off in a “limited preview” for just a “select group of trusted partners and organizations” – meaning, basically, not you.

In a press release announcing the new models, OpenAI said it had notified the U.S. government of its “plans and the models’ capabilities,” and was limiting the rollout of the models “at their request.”

While allowing that the “limited” release for GPT-5.6 will help ensure “the strongest path to broader availability in the coming weeks,” OpenAI warned that “this kind of government access process … keeps the best tools from users, developers, enterprises, cyber defenders, and global partners who need them.”

Anticipating the concerns raised by Anthropic’s Fable and Mythos models, which are said to have breached sensitive national security systems “in hours,” OpenAI went to great lengths to detail GPT 5.6’s “layered” safeguards, including against jailbreaking and “real-world adversarial pressure.”

OpenAI said it anticipates that GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna will be released “soon” to general users. But just as Claude Fable and Mythos remain in a regulatory limbo, it’s not at all clear when the U.S. government will give the all-clear for the GPT-5.6 series to go into wide release.

payload.title: OpenAI rajoittaa GPT-5.6-mallien julkaisua Yhdysvaltain hallinnon pyynnöstä
payload.summary: OpenAI lykkää GPT-5.6-mallien laajaa julkaisua ja avaa ne ensin pienelle, Yhdysvaltain hallinnon ennakkohyväksymälle asiakasjoukolle. Yhtiö sanoo pitävänsä järjestelyä väliaikaisena.
payload.content:
OpenAI rajoittaa seuraavan sukupolven GPT-5.6-tekoälymalliensa julkista käyttöönottoa Yhdysvaltain hallinnon pyynnöstä ja aikoo avata mallit ensin pienelle joukolle asiakkaita, jotka Yhdysvaltain hallinto hyväksyy etukäteen. Yhtiön mukaan saatavuutta on tarkoitus laajentaa tämän jälkeen asteittain, eikä hallinnon kautta kulkevasta käyttöoikeusprosessista pitäisi tulla pysyvää toimintatapaa.

## Julkaisu alkaa rajatusti

OpenAI vahvisti perjantaina, että GPT-5.6-mallien laaja julkaisu viivästyy. Yhtiö sanoi blogikirjoituksessaan pitävänsä rajattua julkaisua lyhyen aikavälin ratkaisuna, jonka se uskoo olevan vahvin reitti laajempaan saatavuuteen tulevien viikkojen aikana.

Yhtiö perusteli kriittistä kantaansa sillä, että hallinnon hyväksyntään perustuva menettely pitää parhaat työkalut poissa käyttäjiltä, kehittäjiltä, yrityksiltä, kyberpuolustajilta ja kansainvälisiltä kumppaneilta, jotka niitä tarvitsevat. OpenAI tekee samalla yhteistyötä hallinnon kanssa kyberturvallisuutta koskevan toimeenpanomääräyksen kehyksen ja tulevia mallijulkaisuja varten toistettavan prosessin kehittämiseksi.

Wiredin mukaan OpenAI ei ole tyytyväinen viivästykseen, mutta yhtiön ajattelua tuntevan henkilön mukaan se pitää hallinnon hyväksyntäprosessia väliaikaisena. The Information raportoi aiemmin OpenAI:n suunnitelmista lykätä seuraavan sukupolven mallien julkaisua Trumpin hallinnon pyynnöstä.

## Turvatoimet ja aikataulu

OpenAI on kuvannut GPT-5.6-mallien suojauksia kerroksellisiksi. Yhtiö on nostanut esiin muun muassa suojautumisen mallien kiertämisyrityksiä vastaan sekä testauksen tilanteissa, joissa mallit joutuvat todellista vihamielistä painetta muistuttaviin olosuhteisiin.

Taustalla on laajempi huoli kehittyneiden tekoälymallien turvallisuudesta. Keskustelua ovat vauhdittaneet Anthropic-yhtiön Fable- ja Mythos-mallit, joiden on kerrottu murtautuneen arkaluonteisiin kansallisen turvallisuuden järjestelmiin tunneissa. Nämä mallit ovat lähteiden mukaan yhä sääntelyyn liittyvässä epävarmuudessa.

OpenAI odottaa, että GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra ja Luna julkaistaan yleisille käyttäjille pian. Yhtiön mukaan tavoitteena on saada GPT-5.6 kaikkien saataville tulevien viikkojen aikana. Vielä ei kuitenkaan ole selvää, milloin Yhdysvaltain hallinto antaa luvan GPT-5.6-sarjan laajalle julkaisulle.

Mallit avataan ensin pienelle, hallinnon ennakkohyväksymälle asiakasjoukolle.
Yhtiö sanoo, ettei hallinnon käyttöoikeusprosessista pitäisi tulla pysyvää oletusmallia.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin neljään lähdeblokkiin. Epävarmaksi jätettiin tarkka laajan julkaisun päivämäärä, koska sitä ei lähteissä vahvistettu.
